sources.title: Fire 400 ka — Pathways to Ancient Britain
sources.supports: The research team distinguishes likely use of wildfires and maintained embers from intentional ignition. Early dates are uncertain; no first discoverer is identified.

sources.title: Davis et al. — Earliest evidence of making fire
sources.supports: The study reports evidence interpreted as deliberate fire-making at Barnham around 400,000 years ago. This evidence date is not a known first invention or discoverer.

sources.title: Berna et al. — Fire evidence at Wonderwerk Cave
sources.supports: Burned bone and plant ash document burning in an archaeological context around one million years ago. This does not identify a person or establish the first ignition method.

clips.title: A cartoon hand cloud reveals fire at the rubbing point
clips.action: From the first frame, one compact classic CARTOON FIGHT CLOUD churns continuously around the monkey's fast-working hands. For0.0–2.3s it stays present and energetic: irregular cream lobes rapidly roll over one another, squash, bulge, fold inward and emerge elsewhere; little puffs peel away while fresh lobes form. Short curved ochre speed strokes whip briefly through the changing cloud. Every new pose changes the cloud silhouette and its internal swirl. Do not repeat a puff cycle, pulse an identical sticker, open expanding smoke rings, or disappear and respawn the whole cloud. This is one sustained frantic action. The two hands rub extremely fast inside it; the monkey's forearms make tiny rapid strokes and its shoulders show concentrated effort. Exactly two sticks stay in contact at their exposed X above the cloud. Keep the monkey's face, supported feet and single tail readable. At2.3–2.7s, the cloud breaks apart and clears ONCE, revealing the two hands still holding the lower stick ends. A modest orange flame catches at the central rubbed X. Its base stays at that exact wood contact, with BOTH remote upper ends remaining unlit. Allow natural flame-height flicker, including brief crowns at or above the tip heights, while keeping the fire compact and rooted at the crossing. Settle to the supplied tiny contact flame in the ending. No large flare, separate torch-tip ignition or fire beside the monkey's face. The monkey stops rubbing and gives one surprised recoil by3.3s, then settles into the supplied ending pose. Preserve slight breathing, a brief blink and tiny contact-flame flicker through5s. No whole-scene freeze.
